transcript.text: roomba e5 wont charge properly, sometimes it does sometimes it doesnt

Intermittent charging is most often poor contact between the robot and dock, followed by a dock/supply issue; an ageing battery is also possible if the contacts and dock prove sound. 1. Switch off and unplug the dock. Wipe the two metal charging strips on the Roomba and the matching contacts on the dock with a dry microfibre cloth. If they are grimy, use a cloth very lightly dampened with isopropyl alcohol, then let everything dry fully. This removes film or oxidation that can make charging come and go. 2. Check the spring-loaded contacts on the dock move freely and return when gently pressed. Do not force them. A sticking contact points to the dock rather than the robot. 3. Plug the dock directly into a known-working wall socket, with its lead fully seated. Put the Roomba on squarely and gently nudge it a few millimetres. If charging only starts in one position, the contacts or dock alignment are the leading cause. If it never starts, the dock supply or robot battery/charging circuit becomes more likely. If cleaning and reseating makes no difference, avoid buying a battery yet: the next useful distinction is whether the dock is most likely providing power, which may need an engineer or a known-good compatible dock to confirm.

ok did that. contacts on the dock were dull with a greasy grey film and loads of hair round the ones on the robot. wiped them with isopropyl and dried. been charging every night for 4 days now, no error. no smell or heat from it either

That points strongly to dirty/contaminated charging contacts rather than a battery or dock fault. Four nights of normal charging with no error after cleaning is a good result. To help prevent it returning, wipe the robot and dock contacts dry every few weeks and keep hair/debris clear from the area around them. If intermittent charging comes back despite clean contacts, then the dock contact springs or battery would be the next things to suspect. Is there anything else you need help with?

candidates: Dirty or oxidised charging contacts, or poor seating on the dock (high)
Dock power supply, lead or wall socket connection (medium)
Ageing robot battery or an internal charging fault (medium)

The fault they reported is: "won't charge properly; charges intermittently". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
